plan.topic: Tirzepatide (Zepbound) for obstructive sleep apnea: what SURMOUNT-OSA showed, with the CHEST 2026 news as the hook
plan.angle:
Answer by 10 s: 'Yes. Tirzepatide (as Zepbound) is FDA-approved, since December 2024, for moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea in adults with obesity.'

Then:
- One AHI number at 52 weeks, tirzepatide vs placebo, from one named SURMOUNT-OSA trial (say whether it was the without-CPAP or with-CPAP trial), with per-arm group sizes from NEJM 2024.
- One line defining AHI: breathing pauses or shallow-breathing events per hour of sleep.
- Safety line: 'If you use CPAP, don't stop or change it on your own; talk to your sleep clinician.'
- One GI side-effects line.
- One CHEST 2026 line: 'At the CHEST 2026 meeting, researchers presented early analyses linking GLP-1 medicines to wider heart and lung benefits in sleep apnea; these are early findings.'
- Prescriber line.

Don't compare GLP-1s with CPAP.
plan.working_title: Tirzepatide (Zepbound): Can It Help Sleep Apnea?
plan.why:
A plain 'Can it…?' question with the drug first and the brand in brackets about an approved use. It fits the proven YouTube pattern and Instagram's preference for yes/no questions, with a fresh hook from CHEST 2026 (Oct 17). | fact-check: The core claim checks out: the FDA approved Zepbound in December 2024 for moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea in adults with obesity. Name Zepbound specifically. Mounjaro isn't approved for sleep apnea, and the working title already uses Zepbound.

The CHEST 2026 items (Managed Healthcare Executive, Oct 17, 2026) were a systematic review of RCTs plus two retrospective TriNetX cohort studies about GLP-1s in general. These are conference abstracts and largely observational, so the one CHEST line needs 'linked to' language and a source credit, and it shouldn't be the evidence for the yes answer.

The angle's line 'it's used alongside CPAP, not as a replacement' isn't label wording. The OSA approval doesn't require CPAP. Recast it as a safety caveat instead (see the safer angle).

Copy the SURMOUNT-OSA AHI numbers, per-arm group sizes and the without-CPAP vs with-CPAP trial from NEJM 2024 (Malhotra et al.).

Source checked: Managed Healthcare Executive (https://www.managedhealthcareexecutive.com/view/more-pluses-for-glp-1s-for-obstructive-sleep-apnea-chest-2026).

package.title: Tirzepatide (Zepbound): Does It Help Sleep Apnea? #shorts
package.description:
Yes. Tirzepatide, as Zepbound, is FDA-approved (Dec 2024) for moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea in adults with obesity, alongside a reduced-calorie diet and more activity. In SURMOUNT-OSA (no CPAP, no diabetes), AHI fell about 25 events an hour over 52 weeks on top tolerated doses of tirzepatide (114 people) vs about 5 on placebo (120 people). Most common side effects were stomach-related, like nausea and diarrhea, mostly mild to moderate. Using CPAP? Don't stop or change it without your sleep clinician.

This content is for educational purposes only and is not medical advice. Always talk to a qualified healthcare professional about your own situation. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

Sources:
1. Malhotra et al., "Tirzepatide for the Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Obesity," NEJM, published online June 21, 2024. https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2404881
2. U.S. FDA, "FDA Approves First Medication for Obstructive Sleep Apnea," Dec 20, 2024. https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-medication-obstructive-sleep-apnea
3. Managed Healthcare Executive, "More pluses for GLP-1s for obstructive sleep apnea | CHEST 2026," Oct 17, 2026. https://www.managedhealthcareexecutive.com/view/more-pluses-for-glp-1s-for-obstructive-sleep-apnea-chest-2026

Zepbound (tirzepatide) is FDA-approved (Dec 2024) for moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea in adults with obesity — here's what the actual trial found.

In SURMOUNT-OSA, AHI (breathing pauses or shallow breaths per hour) fell about 25 events an hour over 52 weeks on top tolerated doses of tirzepatide vs about 5 on placebo — 114 people on tirzepatide, 120 on placebo, none using CPAP, none with diabetes.

New at CHEST 2026: early observational studies linked GLP-1 medicines to higher estimated CPAP use and less acute respiratory failure in sleep apnea — early data, not yet confirmed in trials.

If you're on CPAP, don't stop or change it without your sleep clinician.

factcheck.summary: I checked every claim against the four sources it cites, and all of them hold up. The FDA approved Zepbound on December 20, 2024 "for the treatment of moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) in adults with obesity," "in combination with a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity." That matches s2 and s8. For SURMOUNT-OSA Trial 1 (people not using PAP), the ACC trial summary gives 114 on tirzepatide and 120 on placebo, with AHI changes of −25.3 vs −5.3 events/hour at 52 weeks. So "about 25" vs "about 5" is rounded correctly and each arm is named. NEJM reports that the most common adverse events were gastrointestinal and mostly mild to moderate. That matches s6. The NEJM page returns 403 to automated tools, which is acceptable because the ACC page and NEJM-derived reporting confirm it. The Managed Healthcare Executive CHEST 2026 article (October 17, 2026) describes two retrospective TriNetX cohort studies. One linked GLP-1 use to higher CPAP adherence, measured through proxies. The other linked it to lower acute respiratory failure risk in people with obesity and OSA, and its authors warn against reading cause and effect into it. s7 correctly hedges this as "early observational" and "linked." Safety lines are all there: the CPAP 'don't stop or change' line, a side-effect beat and the full prescriber line. The narration is about 168 words (≤170) and the hook is answered right away. I found three minor wording fixes. Making all three keeps the narration at 170 words or fewer.

issues.claim: AHI fell about 25 events an hour over 52 weeks on tirzepatide
issues.problem: The craft rules say every number needs its trial arm. In SURMOUNT-OSA, people took the maximum tolerated dose (10 or 15 mg). Naming the arm generically is not dosing advice. Adding it pushes the word count over 170 unless the s5 lead-in is trimmed.
issues.fix: s4 narration: "In the SURMOUNT-OSA trial, adults with obesity, no diabetes and no CPAP, AHI fell about 25 events an hour over 52 weeks on top tolerated doses of tirzepatide, versus about 5 on placebo: 114 people on tirzepatide, 120 on placebo." s5 narration: "Using CPAP? Don't stop or change it without your sleep clinician." (Also update the s5 retention_device so it no longer refers to a 'One more thing' re-hook.)

issues.problem: The caption leaves out the approved population (moderate-to-severe OSA in adults with obesity) that the narration gives. That reads broader than the approval when the sound is off.
issues.fix: on_screen_text: "Yes: FDA-approved Dec 2024, adults with obesity"

issues.claim: linked GLP-1 medicines to better CPAP use
issues.problem: The CPAP-adherence study measured use through proxies (the article says the authors 'used proxies of usage'), not directly. 'Better CPAP use' is slightly stronger than that.
issues.fix: "Now the fresh part. At CHEST 2026, early observational studies linked GLP-1 medicines to higher estimated CPAP use and less acute respiratory failure in sleep apnea."

Scene is a bit sparse (sleeping figure + small moon/photo icons) with a lot of empty wall space.

Speech bubble 'Why do I keep pausing?' is cute but the lungs look scared/sweating every frame, which reads a bit distressing for a positive-framed health topic.
Caption 'THAT'S ALONGSIDE A REDUCED-CALORIE' ends on an adjective, splitting the phrase from 'diet' on the next card.
Caption 'THAT'S HOW MANY' ends on the bare word 'MANY' with no noun — confusing fragment.
'AHI' chip label is shown with no expansion anywhere on screen, which is jargon most viewers won't parse in under a second.
Four small blue pause-button icons are scattered around the clock like leftover template UI, not an intentional design element — reads as clutter/bug, not polish.
No labelled hero character, just a clock plus floating icons.
Caption 'THERE WERE ONE' is broken grammar — reads as a mistake, not a sentence.
Caption 'IN THE SURMOUNT-OSA TRIAL,' ends on a trailing comma.
Frame opens on an almost-empty gradient background with only a barely-visible ghosted stat and no hero character/scene for the whole shot — violates the 'headline plus hero' rule.
